answer: Hardware attestation resists sybils: each identity binds to a secure element — a TPM or enclave — that remote-attests one genuine physical device per key, so a single machine cannot mint unlimited identities. Climbing to the summit of participation requires real distinct hardware, marble-solid and scarce, per account. An attacker reaps no nectar from spinning virtual clones, because the attestation proves hardware uniqueness; a thousand fakes would need a thousand real secure devices, a physical cost that does not scale cheaply.
